tasks_attack.title: Mission 1: S3 Basics
tasks_attack.theory: Amazon S3 is a scalable cloud storage service. Threat actors often scan for exposed S3 buckets that allow public access without authentication.
tasks_attack.question: What kind of cloud service is Amazon S3?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 2: Finding Public Buckets
tasks_attack.theory: Public buckets can be discovered via search engines, specialized scanners, or by brute-forcing bucket names. A misconfigured bucket policy causes this exposure.
tasks_attack.question: What type of policy misconfiguration causes exposure?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 3: Exploiting Misconfigurations
tasks_attack.theory: Once an open bucket is found, an attacker can list its contents using the AWS CLI or simply by accessing the bucket URL in a browser.
tasks_attack.question: Which CLI tool can be used to list contents?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 4: Enumerate Bucket
tasks_attack.description: Use terminal: aws s3 ls s3://open-lab-public
tasks_attack.question: What text file is found in the bucket?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 5: Access Sensitive Data
tasks_attack.description: Use terminal: aws s3 cp s3://open-lab-public/secret.txt . && cat secret.txt
tasks_attack.question: What is the exposed key?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 1: IAM Policy
tasks_defence.theory: IAM policies define permissions. To secure S3, apply the principle of least privilege, ensuring anonymous users cannot read bucket contents.
tasks_defence.question: What principle ensures users only have needed permissions?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 2: Blocking Access
tasks_defence.theory: AWS provides a Block Public Access feature that overrides bucket policies and ACLs to ensure no public access is granted.
tasks_defence.question: What AWS feature overrides public bucket policies?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 3: Securing IAM
tasks_defence.theory: Regularly audit IAM roles and remove any wildcard (*) permissions or excessive grants that could allow unintended access.
tasks_defence.question: What symbol represents wildcard permissions?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 4: Check Permissions
tasks_defence.description: Use terminal: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket open-lab-public
tasks_defence.question: What Principal is currently allowed access?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 5: Fix Permissions
tasks_defence.description: Use terminal: aws s3api delete-bucket-policy --bucket open-lab-public
tasks_defence.question: What command deletes the insecure policy?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 1: Scanning Basics
tasks_attack.theory: Network scanning identifies active hosts and available services. Nmap is a primary tool used by attackers for reconnaissance.
tasks_attack.question: What popular tool is used for network scanning?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 2: Finding Open Ports
tasks_attack.theory: Ports act as communication endpoints. Scanning for open ports reveals potential entry points into a system, such as SSH or HTTP.
tasks_attack.question: What port protocol is typically used for web traffic?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 3: Identifying Services
tasks_attack.theory: Service fingerprinting allows an attacker to determine the EXACT software version running on an open port, highlighting known vulnerabilities.
tasks_attack.question: What process determines the software version?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 4: Scan IP
tasks_attack.question: Which port is open for SSH?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 5: Banner Grabbing
tasks_attack.question: What SSH service name was captured?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 1: Detecting Scans
tasks_defence.theory: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) can identify port scans by detecting anomalous connection attempts across multiple ports.
tasks_defence.question: What system identifies anomalous connection attempts?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 2: Closing Ports
tasks_defence.theory: Unused ports must be closed or blocked by a firewall to reduce the attack surface and prevent unauthorized access.
tasks_defence.question: What security device blocks unused ports?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 3: Monitoring Traffic
tasks_defence.theory: Continuous monitoring of network traffic logs helps security operators spot potential threats before they escalate into an attack.
tasks_defence.question: What must be continuously monitored?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 4: View Connections
tasks_defence.question: What state indicates a listening port?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 5: Stop Service
tasks_defence.description: Use terminal to stop the running ncat service.
tasks_defence.question: What command did you use to stop the service?
tasks_defence.hint: Use kill command with service name.

tasks_attack.title: Mission 1: Web Security Basics
tasks_attack.theory: Web application security protects services against threats. Vulnerabilities often happen due to poor input validation.
tasks_attack.question: What causes most web vulnerabilities?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 2: SQL Injection
tasks_attack.theory: SQLi allows an attacker to interfere with application queries.
tasks_attack.question: What does SQLi interfere with?

tasks_attack.title: Mission 3: XSS
tasks_attack.theory: XSS allows an attacker to compromise interactions and steal cookies.
tasks_attack.question: What can an attacker steal?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 1: Input Validation
tasks_defence.theory: Input validation is ensuring data is safe before processing.
tasks_defence.question: What must be done to data?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 2: Parameterized Queries
tasks_defence.theory: To fix SQLi, use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation.
tasks_defence.question: What fixes SQLi?

tasks_defence.title: Mission 3: Content Security Policy
tasks_defence.theory: CSP mitigates XSS by restricting resources.
tasks_defence.question: What policy mitigates XSS?
